# Skewness

> [Anglit][anglit-distribution] distribution [skewness][skewness].

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

The [skewness][skewness] for an [anglit][anglit-distribution] random variable with location parameter `μ` and scale parameter `σ > 0` is

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:anglit_skewness" align="center" raw="\operatorname{skew}\left( X \right) = 0" alt="Skewness for an anglit distribution."> -->

```math
\mathop{\mathrm{skew}}\left( X \right) = 0
```

</section>

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var skewness = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/anglit/skewness' );
```

#### skewness( mu, sigma )

Returns the [skewness][skewness] for an [anglit][anglit-distribution] distribution with location parameter `mu` and scale parameter `sigma`.

```javascript
var y = skewness( 2.0, 1.0 );
// returns 0.0

y = skewness( 0.0, 1.0 );
// returns 0.0

y = skewness( -1.0, 4.0 );
// returns 0.0
```

If provided `NaN` as any argument, the function returns `NaN`.

```javascript
var y = skewness( NaN, 1.0 );
// returns NaN

y = skewness( 0.0, NaN );
// returns NaN
```

If provided `sigma <= 0`, the function returns `NaN`.

```javascript
var y = skewness( 0.0, 0.0 );
// returns NaN

y = skewness( 0.0, -1.0 );
// returns NaN
```

</section>

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var logEachMap = require( '@stdlib/console/log-each-map' );
var skewness = require( '@stdlib/stats/base/dists/anglit/skewness' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float64'
};
var mu = uniform( 10, -5.0, 5.0, opts );
var sigma = uniform( 10, 0.1, 20.0, opts );

logEachMap( 'μ: %lf, σ: %lf, skew(X;μ,σ): %lf', mu, sigma, skewness );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<!-- C usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/stats/base/dists/anglit/skewness.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_dists_anglit_skewness( mu, sigma )

Returns the skewness for an anglit distribution with location parameter `mu` and scale parameter `sigma`.

```c
double out = stdlib_base_dists_anglit_skewness( 0.0, 1.0 );
// returns 0.0
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **mu**: `[in] double` location parameter.
-   **sigma**: `[in] double` scale parameter.

```c
double stdlib_base_dists_anglit_skewness( const double mu, const double sigma );
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- C API usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/stats/base/dists/anglit/skewness.h"
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>

static double random_uniform( const double min, const double max ) {
    double v = (double)rand() / ( (double)RAND_MAX + 1.0 );
    return min + ( v*(max-min) );
}

int main( void ) {
    double sigma;
    double mu;
    double y;
    int i;

    for ( i = 0; i < 10; i++ ) {
        mu = random_uniform( -5.0, 5.0 );
        sigma = random_uniform( 0.1, 20.0 );
        y = stdlib_base_dists_anglit_skewness( mu, sigma );
        printf( "μ: %lf, σ: %lf, skew(X;μ,σ): %lf\n", mu, sigma, y );
    }
}
```

</section>
